purpose: Search the Walker-Delta phasing factor F for Starlink Phase 2-a to see if any integer value reproduces the paper's published peak accessible-satellite count of 27 (Fig. 5 / N_max).
method: ilcho.sanity.max_accessible_vs_latitude equivalent, per F: global peak accessible-satellite count over latitudes 0-90deg (lon0=40, duration_s=6000, dt=20s, min_elev=30deg), swapping only phasing_factor via dataclasses.replace on the Phase 2-a ConstellationConfig
result_summary: No F in [0,47] reproduces 27. Range observed: 29-32. F=1 (the value used throughout the reproduction) already yields the minimum achievable peak (29) in this search space.
conclusion: The 27 vs 29 mismatch is not explained by the unpublished Walker phasing factor F. It must come from some other unpublished detail of the paper's methodology (peak-counting convention, temporal sampling resolution, RAAN/epoch offset, or a different Walker phasing convention).
peak_latitude_deg: 50.0 for every F tested (the latitude of the peak did not shift)
